LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about chores and fun activities.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#1 Introductions Song
•	 TR#5 Days of the Week Song
•	 TR#7 After-School Activities Song
•	 TR#9 Prepositions Actions Song
•	 TR#10 Puppy Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home
•	 Calendar (P.E.M.1)
•	 After-School Activities (P.E.M.2)
•	 Days of the Week cards (P.E.M.5)

(P.1.5)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 4: Fun Activity cards (P.1.2)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 6: Number cards (P.E.M.3)

BEFORE CLASS
SCHOOL
P&P S1 | Page 3

Prepare and label your Ss’ material beforehand. 
•	 Prepare and label the right number of bags.
•	 Prepare and label the right number of Story 1 Student 
Books.
•	 Tear the Story 1 stickers through the dotted line.
Prepare the stickers for p.3 of the Student Book.
LESSON PLAN
1.– WARM-UP ROUTINES (10’)
•	 Hello + calling the register
•	 Calendar (P.E.M.1)
•	 After-School Activities, TR#7
Introduce yourself to the Ss and welcome them to the 
Pam&Paul course. Call the register. Then do the Calendar and 
the After-School Activities routines. Please, see the Warm-Up 
routines index for further instructions on how to proceed with 
this part.
2.– INTRODUCTIONS SONG (TR#1) (5’)
Say, “It’s time to introduce ourselves. Let me teach you 
the Introductions Song!”. Model the choreography and sing 
the song at a slower pace without playing the music. You can 
introduce yourself first, so the Ss get the gist of the activity.
Then get the Ss to stand up and sing the Introductions Song 
following the instructions in the note below.
INTRODUCTIONS SONG
Everywhere we go
People always ask us
Who we are
And where we are from
So we tell them
My name is…
My surname is…
I am from... (x10)
NOTE: this song is recorded with short musical interludes for 
the Ss to take turns introducing themselves. This is repeated 
10 times, but you can stop the song once each S has had a 
turn singing. You can use a toy microphone to get the Ss to 
complete the sentences. They can also sing while clapping 
their hands to the rhythm of “We will rock you”.

3.– STORY (PP.2-7) (8’)
Tell the Ss the first half of the story using the Big Book. Please 
see the section on storytelling in the Warm-Up Routines Index.
4.– ACTIVITY 8: DAYS OF THE WEEK SONG (TR#5) (5’)
P.1.5
Monday
> Warm-Up
To begin with, take the Days of the Week flash cards from Act. 
5 (P.1.5). Ask, “What’s the first day of the week?”. Encourage 
Ss to say, “It’s Monday.”
Then place the Monday flash card up on the whiteboard and 
ask, “What comes after Monday?”, to which Ss should answer 
“After Monday comes Tuesday.”. If the Ss aren’t sure, show 
them the flash cards and ask: “Is it Friday? Is it Wednesday?” 
etc. Continue until you’ve placed all the Days of the Week cards 
on the board in order.
> Main Activity
Sing and dance to the song following the instructions written 
in brackets. 
DAYS OF THE WEEK SONG
(Ss sitting on the floor and whispering)
Monday, Tuesday
Here we come,
Wednesday, Thursday,
Let’s get it done! (Ss fist-pump the air)
Friday is here,
We’re ready to cheer! (Ss stand up)
Here comes the weekend,
Hip hip hurray! (Ss cheer)
Saturday, Sunday,
They are both cool days! (Ss dance)

Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday,
Saturday aaand Sunday! (repeat) 
(pointing to the different days of the week cards on the 
board)
NOTE: for the last part of the choreography, you can also 
give each S a day card and have them show it when the day 
is mentioned in the last two verses.

NOTE: use this opportunity to give your Ss their book. Have 
them ask you for it by saying “Can I have my book, please?”. 
Explain the activity before giving out the books since the Ss 
might get distracted.
In this activity, the Ss must use the stickers to create their 
weekly after-school activities schedule. Start by reviewing the 
activities depicted on the stickers by asking, “What’s this?” 
and eliciting, “This is going to be football practice or football 
training.” Do not give out the stickers yet.
Now, pair the children up and explain that they must ask each 
other what they do after school. Model the task by asking a S, 
“John, what do you do on Mondays?” to which the S must answer, 
“On Mondays, I go to football practice/training.”. Explain that, 
once John answers, he will have to place the football practice 
sticker on the Monday column of his worksheet.
Have them ask you for the stickers by saying, “Can I have 
some stickers, please?”.
You can have the pairs of Ss sit on the floor or at the table(s) 
around the room so that they have enough space to work. Tell 
your Ss that they have only five minutes to do this activity. 
Some children might do activities that aren’t on the stickers, in 
which case they can draw what they do on their grid instead. 
While they are completing the activity, walk around the room 
and listen to make sure that they are speaking English and 
help them if needed.

When the time is up, ask them to come back to the table, even 
if they haven’t filled in the whole grid. Ask each S a follow-up 
question about their partner’s routine and elicit full answers. 
Follow this model:
•	 T: “John, what does Jane do on Mondays?”
•	 John: “On Mondays, Jane goes to football practice/
training.”
If time allows, ask each S a question about their partner’s 
after-school activities.
NOTE: ask the Ss to give you their books back by saying “Can 
I have your books, please?”. We give them their materials at the 
end of the lesson, and we do not want them to get distracted 
with their student book.

7.– ACTIVITY 4: CHARADES (VERSION 1) (8’)
P.1.2

> Warm-Up
Quickly drill the Fun Activities (P.1.2). Show the cards one by 
one and point to one of your Ss saying the action, for example, 
“Jane is watching TV.”. In this case, Jane will have to mime 
watching TV.
> Main Activity
A S takes a card showing one fun activity (P.1.2). They must 
mime the action and ask, “What am I doing?”. The others must 
guess by asking, “Are you watching TV?” and the S miming 
must respond either, “No, I’m not.” or “Yes, I am.”. Do as many 
rounds as time allows.
8.– ACTIVITY 6: NUMBERS (VERSION 1) (6’)
P.E.M.3
55
> Warm-Up
Review the numbers using the Number cards (P.E.M.3) 
without the jokers. Ask, “What number is this?” and have the 
Ss answer, “It’s number…”. Review some of the numbers from 
50 to 99 all together as a group. It might be your Ss’ first time 
learning numbers over 50, so we recommend reviewing them 
in order at first.
> Main Activity
The goal is to find as many cards as possible. Stick some of 
the Number cards (P.E.M.3) on the wall (out of reach of the Ss, 
so they can’t damage them). Say, “Find number...” and have 
the Ss run and point to the corresponding number. When the 
S points to the correct number, take it off the wall and keep it 
as a point for that S. The S who collects the most cards wins. 
NOTE: this game can become hectic if everybody is playing 
at the same time. It is advisable to play this game in duels of 
two Ss (S1 vs S2). You call out the number and the two Ss must 
race to point to the card first.

Say, “I have got something very special to give you. These 
are your Pam&Paul materials!” as you show them the materials.
Then say, “These are your new special books. As you can see, 
they have got worksheets inside;” (flip through the worksheet 
section) “these are activities we will do in class all together.”
Then say, “And they also have special sticker pages!”. Show 
them the first sticker page and the stickers for Day 1, ask “What 
are these?”, and elicit “They are stickers!”. Explain, “Each week, 
I’ll give you a set of stickers. At home, you’ll have to find the 
correct number and stick each sticker on its spot!”
Finally, turn to pp.29-30 and show them their booklet. Say, 
“Look, this is your new booklet! At home, you will visit a very 
special place called My Way. There, you can listen to the track. 
Every time you listen to it, you must colour in one picture.” 
Finish by saying the following mysteriously, “Today, you must 
log in to My Way and meet your new virtual pet! If you want 
to play with it, you must listen to the audio track first! Then 
you have to start Mission 1. You can play four mission games 
this week!”
At this point, give them their bags, their book, and the Day 
1 stickers. Have them ask for each item as a group by saying 
“Can I have...?”
10.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (1’)
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class.

BONUS
ACTIVITY 1: MY CHORES
P.1.1
P.1.1
P.1.1
TARGET LANGUAGE FOR FUN ACTIVITIES
Play video games
Read a book
Listen to music
Talk on the phone
Watch TV
Draw a picture
Ride my bike
Play football
Roller-skate
Play in the park
TARGET LANGUAGE FOR CHORES
Wash Billy
Feed Billy
Take Billy for a walk
Brush Billy
Give Billy some water
Pick up Billy’s poo
Lay the table
Make the bed
Take out the rubbish
Sweep the floor
Clear the table 
> How to Play
Ss must find the activities that match those on their bingo 
board. In order to win, the Ss must find all their chores first, 
and then their fun activity.
> Warm-Up
Start by drilling the target language. Spread the Chores cards 
(P.1.1) on the table and say: “Wow! Look at my chores. I have 
a lot of things to do! I have to feed Billy (signal to the Ss to 
repeat after you), wash Billy, etc.” 
Now review the fun activities. Start by saying: “This is what I 
want to do. I want to...”. Show the Ss the fun activity cards one 
by one and let them finish the sentence with the fun activity.

> Main Activity
Hand out an A5 Bingo board (P.1.1) to each S. Then spread 
out the Memory cards, which show the chores and fun activities 
(P.1.1), face down on the table.
Choose a S to go first. You can check out the different tips on 
how to start a game at the beginning of this guide. The S turns 
over a Memory card and identifies the activity by saying one of 
the following phrases depending on the scenario:
•	 If they have it: “I have to...”
•	 If they don’t have it: “I don’t have to...”
•	 If they find a fun activity before their chores: “I can’t ... 
now, I must ... first.” For instance: “I can’t play video 
games now, I must wash the puppy, clear the table 
and make the bed first.”
The first S to collect all their chores followed by their fun 
activity is the winner.
> Follow-Up
Once you have finished the activity, point to the winner’s 
board and ask the Ss, “What chores must Jane do first?” to 
which they should reply “Jane must clear the table, take out 
the rubbish and make the bed first and then she can listen 
to music.”
ACTIVITY 9: PREPOSITIONS (TR#9)
> Warm-Up
The Ss should perform the following actions to rehearse 
the movements.
•	 March in line. (all the Ss march in a single file line)
•	 Hide under the table.
•	 Walk next to a friend.
•	 Stand between two chairs.
•	 Jump behind the teacher. (all the Ss jump on the spot 
behind the teacher)
•	 Run in front of the (white) board. (all the Ss run on 
the spot in front of the board)
•	 Sit on a chair.
> Main Activity
Then play the Prepositions Actions Song (TR#9) and dance 
to it.
PREPOSITIONS ACTIONS SONG
(as you sing, simply perform the actions mentioned in the song. 
You can also create a hand choreography for the preposition 
verses.)

In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop. 
March in line, in, in line. 
(musical interlude)
Hide under the table, under, under the table.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Walk next to a friend, next to, next to a friend. 
(musical interlude)
Stand between two chairs, between, between two chairs.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop. 
 
Jump behind the teacher, behind, behind the teacher. 
(musical interlude)
Run in front of the board, in front of, in front of the board.  
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
In, on, under, next to, between, in front of, behind. 
Now stop.  
Sit on a chair, on, on a chair. 
(musical interlude)
This is the end, the end, the end.
